key_insight: A lightweight test-time adaptation (TTA) framework built on a Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) enables robust, low-overhead correction for EMG signal drift (electrode shifts, fatigue, posture) so gesture recognition models maintain accuracy over long-term use on energy‑constrained wearables.
problem_solved: Mitigates sharp performance degradation of EMG-based gesture classifiers caused by non-stationary signals in real-world, long-term use without requiring large retraining datasets or heavy compute pipelines.
method: Use a compact Temporal Convolutional Network to capture short- and long-range temporal patterns in streaming EMG data.

Apply lightweight, online test-time adaptation updates (unsupervised/self-supervised objectives) to a small subset of model parameters so the system adapts to signal drift with minimal compute and memory overhead.
Design the pipeline for edge deployment: low-latency updates, small model footprint, and energy-efficient operations suited for wearable devices.
impact: Enables more reliable, long-term EMG gesture decoding on resource-constrained wearables, reducing the need for frequent recalibration or large offline datasets and making practical on-device personalization feasible.
visual_elements: Diagram: wearable armband → EMG signal stream → TCN + TTA module → predicted gesture, illustrating online adaptation loop
Chart: accuracy over time comparing baseline (no adaptation) vs. lightweight TTA showing stable performance under electrode shift/fatigue events
Block diagram: small TCN architecture highlighting the few parameters updated during test-time (low compute/memory)
Icon set: wearable device, low-power chip, drifted signal waveform, adaptation/refresh arrow to convey robustness and edge suitability
paper_title: Lightweight Test-Time Adaptation for EMG-Based Gesture Recognition
paper_authors: Nia Touko, Matthew O A Ellis, Cristiano Capone, Alessio Burrello, Elisa Donati
